calls.title: scott@growthbook.io - Fri, 22 May 2026 11:01:44 EDT - Untitled
calls.summary: Enrique Hoyos is leading initiatives to automate AI-driven experimentation and feature flag management to reduce manual effort and accelerate testing. The discussion highlighted the automation of data analysis for conversion improvement, utilizing Growth Book and Snowflake APIs for accurate experiment tracking, and addressing complexities arising from managing numerous feature flags. Automation challenges were noted, particularly concerning higher-risk experiments that require manual approval. Both speakers shared insights on the future vision of AI in streamlining processes while ensuring human oversight, and the need for user feedback to enhance product features and workflows. Techniques for better audience segmentation and managing experiment overlaps were also discussed.
calls.keywords: Growth Book, AI automation, feature flags, experiment targeting, data warehouse, Cursor

calls.title: scott@growthbook.io - Wed, 25 Mar 2026 11:02:34 EDT - Untitled
calls.summary: The discussion highlighted the composition of experimentation teams, typically blending product, analytics, and engineering roles, with larger organizations sometimes employing dedicated test managers. It emphasized the transition of centralized experimentation teams from governance to enabling stakeholder self-service, allowing for scalability. A key example was Peacock, which increased its experimentation from under 50 to over 750 through effective training and system integration. The meeting also examined market maturity, noting that many organizations conduct fewer than 100 experiments annually due to engineering constraints. Budgeting for experimentation usually falls to engineering teams, while product teams manage experiments without direct budget control. Finally, the need for refining ideal customer profiles through data was underscored, alongside the development of a shared repository for tracking client team structures.
calls.keywords: Experimentation team structure, governance, self-service enablement, CMS integration, product vs. marketing experiments, ICP targeting, tooling teams, maturity model
